fatal_errors: The cited AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 study does not isolate Ti doping against an undoped CoCrFeNi control, so it cannot support the claimed causal effect of approximately 5 at.% Ti.
No evidence is provided that Ti forms a continuous low-shear or spinel-type lubricious oxide; common Ti oxides are not inherently established as low-shear lubricants.
The hypothesis does not substantiate low friction and wear throughout the full temperature range, particularly the challenging intermediate-temperature regime.
explanation: The proposal addresses the general CoCrFeNi wide-temperature tribology problem and offers a testable single intervention, but it does not reconstruct the target intervention of varying Mo in a Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite. It also omits the specified SPS processing and ball-on-disk conditions, Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze. Its baseline, loads, and environmental limits are insufficiently defined. The controlled comparison and falsification rule are reasonably discriminating, although testing only room temperature, 500 °C, and 800 °C could miss the 200–400 °C degradation maximum. Most importantly, E1 only shows temperature-dependent behavior of a composition containing substantial Al and Ti; it neither demonstrates that adding Ti to CoCrFeNi causes the improvement nor validates the proposed lubricious oxide mechanism.
